DGF.Settings.autoSuspicion.Name: Raise Suspicion automatically
DGF.Settings.autoSuspicion.Hint: Each roll's Suspicion (one roll, one rise: its biggest trigger) goes on the Raid HUD as soon as it is rolled. Off: the Storyteller applies it from the roll card.
DGF.Settings.autoCharges.Name: Spend charges automatically
DGF.Settings.autoCharges.Hint: Abilities on a roll spend their charges (a helper's too), and a Critical gives one spent charge back. Off: players keep their charges by hand.
DGF.Settings.autoForm.Name: Jekyll becomes Hyde automatically
DGF.Settings.autoForm.Hint: When the Monster shows on one of Jekyll's rolls, the sheet changes to Hyde's dice. Off: the card says so and the player drinks the Draught by hand.
DGF.Settings.autoCosts.Name: Apply the Storyteller's Cost
DGF.Settings.autoCosts.Hint: When the Storyteller picks a Cost on a roll card it applies itself: Suspicion +1 on the HUD, the dropped item leaves the sheet, the lost Turn or the smaller die is marked on the Entity. Off: the card only records the choice.
DGF.Settings.autoHunt.Name: Start the hunt automatically
DGF.Settings.autoHunt.Hint: At the Limit, or when dawn comes, the whole town hunts: Suspicion stops and the Mask is off. Off: the Storyteller starts it from the HUD.
DGF.Settings.hudVisible.Name: Show the Raid HUD
DGF.Settings.hudVisible.Hint: A small window for everyone with Suspicion, the Limit and the Turn. The Storyteller's copy has the controls.
DGF.Settings.showOdds.Name: Show the odds when rolling
DGF.Settings.showOdds.Hint: The roll dialog shows the chance of each result (for this player only).
DGF.Notify.noGM: The Storyteller isn't connected — nothing was changed.
DGF.Notify.opFailed: The Storyteller's client didn't answer — nothing was changed.
DGF.Notify.notOwner: You can only roll for your own Entity.
DGF.Notify.refused: The Storyteller's client turned that down — nothing was changed.
DGF.Roll.title: {name} rolls
DGF.Roll.abilities: Abilities (one charge each, spent before you roll)
DGF.Roll.abilityHint: At most one raise per roll, Castle Duty included. At zero charges an ability still works: that's an overdraw.
DGF.Roll.helpers: Help from the others at the same place (their charge)
DGF.Roll.duty: Castle Duty ({duty}): this location's list item is {kind}, so the trait die is one size larger
DGF.Roll.loud: The loud way (Suspicion +1 whatever the result)
DGF.Roll.companionCarrying: Someone with you carries loot or furniture (Out of Sight: then Trouble gets you caught; your own carrying and a helper's count by themselves)
DGF.Roll.wayOut: The way out of town (Difficulty {difficulty}, always watched)
DGF.Roll.notice.hunt: The whole town hunts: the Mask is off and Suspicion has stopped.
DGF.Roll.notice.carrying: Carrying furniture: no Mask, and Nimble is one size smaller.
DGF.Roll.notice.smaller: A Cost: this roll's trait die is one size smaller ({n}).
DGF.Roll.notice.skipTurn: A Cost: this Entity loses Turn {turn}.
DGF.Roll.notice.weakness: The Weakness is in play: the trait die is one size smaller in a chase, and no overdraw.
DGF.Roll.notice.spectral: Spectral: past {label} without rolling (it carries nothing). This roll isn't part of the group check.
DGF.Roll.notice.notInRaid: This Entity isn't in this raid: the Storyteller can add it on the Raid window.
DGF.Effect.raise: raise a trait die one size
DGF.Effect.switch: use {trait} instead of the trait called
DGF.Effect.hidden: roll the Monster die without risking Suspicion
DGF.Effect.open: open an approach with {trait} (2 lower Difficulty)
DGF.Effect.openWatched: open an approach with {trait} where someone’s watching (2 lower Difficulty; tick Watched first)
DGF.Plan.badDie: This Entity's {trait} die isn't one of d4–d12.
DGF.Plan.helpInLocalChase: In a local chase, abilities help only your own roll.
DGF.Plan.twoTraits: Only one trait can be rolled: use one ability that changes it.
DGF.Plan.openInChase: An approach of your own can't be opened in a chase.
DGF.Plan.openByHelper: {name} opens an approach only for the one who uses it.
DGF.Plan.noLootThroughWall: {name}: nothing you carry passes through. Hand over or drop the loot and furniture first.
DGF.Plan.maskOffHunt: Once the hunt is on, the Mask is off: rolling the Monster.
DGF.Plan.maskCarrying: Carriers can't use the Mask: rolling the Monster.
DGF.Plan.tooManyRaises: At most one raise per roll, from any source, Castle Duty included.
DGF.Plan.raiseLost: A d12 can't go higher: the raise is lost.
DGF.Plan.stepLost: Nothing goes below a d4: the extra step down is lost.
DGF.Plan.hiddenWithMask: Rolling without risking Suspicion only matters with the Monster die.
DGF.Plan.overdrawWeakness: {name} can't overdraw while its Weakness is in play.
DGF.Plan.overdrawOnce: {name} has already overdrawn in this flight: once per flight.
DGF.Plan.captiveOnlySlips: Held at the lock-up: its one roll is slipping free (tick “At the lock-up”).
DGF.Plan.lockupInHunt: The whole town hunts: everyone who isn't captured is in the final flight.
DGF.Plan.openListed: {name} opens an approach only with a trait this obstacle doesn't list.
DGF.Plan.openNotWatched: {name} opens an approach only where someone's watching: tick Watched (the way out and the lock-up always are).
DGF.Plan.notListed.wayOut: The way out takes Sly or Nimble, or Brawn the loud way.
DGF.Plan.notListed.rescue: The lock-up takes Sly, or Brawn the loud way.
DGF.Plan.notListed.slip: Slipping free takes Sly or Nimble, or Brawn the loud way.
DGF.Plan.notOnGround: This round the ground lets you roll {traits}.
DGF.Plan.slipTooSoon: A captive may first try to slip free on the Turn after its capture.
DGF.Plan.slipOncePerTurn: A captive tries to slip free once per Turn.
DGF.Card.overdrawWeakness: {name} overdraws: its Weakness is in play from its next roll
DGF.Card.huntStops: — the hunt is on: Suspicion has stopped
DGF.Card.monsterUnseen: The Monster shows, unseen: it raises nothing.
DGF.Card.hydeWouldTakeOver: Hyde takes over (automatic changes of form are off: drink the Draught on the sheet).
DGF.Card.caught: Caught! Someone was watching: a local chase starts (Chapter 6).
DGF.Card.unseen: Watched, but nobody can see him, and nobody with him carries loot or furniture: no chase (Out of Sight).
DGF.Card.seen.self: Out of Sight, but he carries loot or furniture: they can see a floating candlestick.
DGF.Card.seen.helper: Out of Sight, but {name}, helping him, carries loot or furniture.
DGF.Card.seen.companion: Out of Sight, but someone with him carries loot or furniture.
DGF.Card.dropped: drops {item} here; picking it up costs an action
DGF.Card.nextSmaller: the next roll's trait die is one size smaller
DGF.Card.free: Changing back to Jekyll costs no charge.
DGF.Card.noCost: Cost — nothing here would cost anything right now.
DGF.RaidCard.newRaid.title: A new raid
DGF.RaidCard.hunt.title: The whole town hunts
DGF.RaidCard.hunt.text: {cause}. Suspicion stops and the Mask is off: everyone who isn't captured flees together in the final flight (Chapter 6).
DGF.RaidCard.dawn.title: Dawn
DGF.RaidCard.dawn.text: The last Turn has ended. Anyone still in town runs for it in the final flight.
DGF.RaidCard.limit.title: At the Limit
DGF.RaidCard.limit.text: Suspicion has reached the Limit ({limit}): the whole town hunts. Start the hunt on the Raid HUD.
DGF.Create.title: New Entity
DGF.Create.replace: Replace this Entity's dice and picks with the book's defaults for the new one?
DGF.Create.hint: Filled with the book's dice and marked defaults; change the picks on the sheet.
DGF.Sheet.label: Entity sheet
DGF.Sheet.warn.duplicate: Another Entity in this world is the same one: no two players play the same Entity.
DGF.Sheet.warn.duty: Another Entity has this Castle Duty: the second player picks another (or rolls a d6 again).
DGF.Sheet.dutyText: Shops for {kind}: {where}. At a location whose list item is this kind, your trait die is one size larger on your own rolls (the roll's one raise).
DGF.Sheet.mark.smaller: Next roll's trait die one size smaller ({n})
DGF.Sheet.noEntity: Choose which of the eight Entities this is.
DGF.Sheet.rollHint: Click a trait to roll it.
DGF.Sheet.draughtHint: Change form; the new form lasts until the next draught.
DGF.Overdraw.title: Overdraw
DGF.Overdraw.suspicion: {name} has no charges left. Use the ability anyway, for Suspicion +{n}?
DGF.Overdraw.weakness: {name} has no charges left. Use the ability anyway? Its Weakness will be in play from its next roll to the end of the flight.
DGF.Raid.title: The Raid
DGF.Raid.newRaidText: Start a new raid: Suspicion back to 0, Turn 1. How hard is the town?
DGF.Raid.up: Suspicion +1 (a Tell, or anything you judge)
DGF.Settings.autoChase.Name: Run chases automatically
DGF.Settings.autoChase.Hint: A caught Entity's local chase starts by itself, the hunt starts the final flight, the ground is rolled each round, the Lead moves by the rolls (the majority rule when several flee together) and the chase ends at the escape number or at 0. Off: the Storyteller does each step on the chase tracker.
DGF.Settings.autoLockup.Name: Run the lock-up automatically
DGF.Settings.autoLockup.Hint: Cornered in a local chase, an Entity is captured and the town takes back what it carried; a captive's slip-free roll and a rescue free them by themselves. Off: the Storyteller changes the Entities' status by hand.
DGF.Settings.autoGroupChecks.Name: Group checks
DGF.Settings.autoGroupChecks.Hint: The Storyteller can open a group check on the Raid HUD: its rolls raise Suspicion once, by the biggest trigger among them, and everyone caught in it flees together. Off: every roll stands alone and the Storyteller cancels the extra rises by hand.
DGF.Settings.autoYear.Name: Offer how the year went
DGF.Settings.autoYear.Hint: When the party gets out (the way out beaten, or the final flight escaped) a card asks the Storyteller what came home; when the party is forked, the year card posts itself. Off: use End the raid on the Raid HUD.
DGF.Settings.autoFurniture.Name: Carried furniture raises Suspicion each Turn
DGF.Settings.autoFurniture.Hint: From the Turn a piece of furniture is first taken until it leaves town, is lost or is abandoned, Suspicion rises by 1 at the end of each Turn (Next Turn on the Raid HUD), even while it is set down. Off: the Storyteller adds it by hand.
DGF.Settings.resetOnNewRaid.Name: A new raid resets the Entities
DGF.Settings.resetOnNewRaid.Hint: A new raid is a new year: every Entity is free again, its charges refill, and the last raid's marks (a lost Turn, a smaller die, the Weakness) go.
DGF.Settings.chaseTracker.Name: Open the chase tracker when a chase starts
DGF.Settings.chaseTracker.Hint: Everyone's chase tracker opens by itself at the start of each chase. Off: open it from the Raid HUD.
DGF.Roll.notice.chase: {kind}, round {round}: {ground}. Roll {traits} against the mob's Difficulty {mob}.
DGF.Roll.notice.chaseWeakness: The mob has brought this Entity's Weakness: its trait die is one size smaller for the rest of the chase.
DGF.Roll.lockupSlip: At the lock-up: slipping free (Difficulty {difficulty}; Sly or Nimble, or Brawn the loud way)
DGF.Roll.lockupRescue: At the lock-up: a rescue (Difficulty {difficulty}; Sly, or Brawn the loud way; always watched)
DGF.Roll.furniture: The furniture's extra obstacle, at the Difficulty rolled for it (this adds the 2 harder, at most 12; a premade town prints it 2 harder already, so leave this off there)
DGF.Plan.noGround: The ground for this round isn't rolled yet.
DGF.Plan.alreadyRolled: This Entity has already rolled this round of the chase.
DGF.Card.majority: on its own; the shared Lead moves by the majority rule
DGF.Card.slipFree: Slips free! It acts again next Turn.
DGF.Card.slipTrouble: Still held: Suspicion rises, but no chase starts.
DGF.Card.rescued: The lock-up is beaten: every captive there is free and acts again next Turn.
DGF.Card.wayOutBeaten: The way out is beaten: everyone who isn't captured gets out.
DGF.Card.chaseStarted: The local chase is on (see the chase tracker).
DGF.RaidCard.group.title: A group check
DGF.RaidCard.group.text: {what}: {names} declare their dice and abilities, then roll together. Suspicion rises once, by the biggest trigger among their rolls; everyone caught flees together.
DGF.RaidCard.group.spectralRolls: {names} carries loot or furniture, so Spectral doesn't get it past: it rolls like anyone else.
DGF.RaidCard.groupClosed.title: The group check is closed
DGF.RaidCard.list.title: The shopping list
DGF.RaidCard.list.text: {label}: everything the castle needs this year.
DGF.RaidCard.home.title: Out of town
DGF.RaidCard.home.flight: The party outran the mob: home with the goods.
DGF.RaidCard.home.wayOut: The party is out of town.
DGF.RaidCard.home.nobody: The whole town hunts, but nobody is free to flee.
DGF.RaidCard.backInTown.title: Back in town
DGF.RaidCard.backInTown.text: The Storyteller takes back the party's leaving: they are still in town, and the raid goes on. The hunt and chases can start again.
DGF.RaidCard.backInTown.piece: The furniture is in play again (it was taken): Suspicion +1 at the end of each Turn until it really leaves town, is lost or abandoned.
DGF.Chase.title: The Chase
DGF.Chase.outcome.local.escaped: Clear! Back where they were caught, with the Turn used up.
DGF.Chase.outcome.local.ended: The whole town hunts: this chase ends, and they join the final flight.
DGF.Chase.outcome.local.dropped: The Storyteller called the chase off.
DGF.Chase.outcome.final.dropped: The Storyteller called the flight off.
DGF.Chase.fate.captured: {name} is captured and held at the lock-up.
DGF.Chase.fate.loseTurn: {name} loses its next Turn instead of being captured (Already Dead).
DGF.Chase.fate.forked: Forked: the monsters are killed and the raid is lost.
DGF.Chase.taken: The town takes back what it was carrying: {items}.
DGF.Chase.kept: It keeps what it carries: {items} (Hidden Pockets).
DGF.Chase.startText: {cause}. The Lead starts at {lead}; clear at {escape}, cornered at 0.
DGF.Chase.weakLine: The mob has brought their Weakness: {names} (trait die one size smaller).
DGF.Chase.noGround: The ground for this round isn't rolled yet.
DGF.Chase.weaknessTip: The mob has brought this Entity's Weakness: its trait die is one size smaller.
DGF.Chase.majorityHint: Shared Lead: Successes against Trouble (a Critical counts as two). One more: the Lead moves 1; two or more: it moves 2.
DGF.Chase.refused.chaseRunning: A chase is already running: finish it first (the chase tracker), then start this one.
DGF.Chase.refused.huntOn: The whole town hunts: everyone who isn't captured is in the final flight.
DGF.Chase.refused.partyOut: The party is out of town: no chase starts now.
DGF.Tell.title: A Tell check
DGF.Tell.intro: The first time anyone reaches a watched location (the way out and the lock-up included), check once, however the party has split. Who is arriving?
DGF.Tell.familiar: Familiar's Warning: the second d6 must also roll 4–6.
DGF.Tell.refused.alreadyChecked: That watched location has already had its Tell check.
DGF.Group.title: A group check
DGF.Group.intro: Several Entities roll the same group obstacle this Turn: they declare their dice and abilities, then roll together. Who is rolling?
DGF.Group.refused.tooFew: Tick at least two Entities: a group check is several rolling together.
DGF.Group.refused.groupOpen: A group check is already open: close it on the Raid HUD first.
DGF.Group.refused.groupChecksOff: Group checks are switched off (Configure Settings).
DGF.List.title: The shopping list
DGF.List.intro: {label}: {size} items, rolled on the shopping table (a d6 for the kind, a d6 for the item; a repeat is rolled again). The first rolled are the essentials.
DGF.Year.title: How the year went: {result}
DGF.Year.furniture: A piece of furniture came home too.
DGF.Year.left: Left behind at the lock-up ({n}): {names}. Each drops the result one step.
DGF.Year.intro: What came home? Tick each item on the list that did. (Ticked to start with: the items the Entities who got out are carrying.)
DGF.Year.noList: No shopping list was rolled: fill in the items and their kinds.
DGF.Year.furnitureHome: A piece of furniture or decor came home
DGF.Year.leftBehind: Entities left behind at the lock-up
DGF.Year.forked: Forked: cornered in the final flight
DGF.Year.already: The year is already decided. Start a new raid on the Raid HUD.
DGF.Year.refused.badList: Every item needs one of the six kinds.
DGF.Year.refused.emptyList: Fill in the shopping list first.
DGF.Chase.furnitureLost: The furniture it carried is lost for the night.
DGF.Card.roundRise: (in a shared chase, Suspicion rises once a round, by the biggest trigger)
DGF.List.essentialsByDie: How many essentials: a d6, odd one, even two.
DGF.List.essentialsRolled: Essentials: a d6 rolled {face} (odd one, even two): {n}.
DGF.Year.furnitureLost: The furniture was lost or abandoned for the night: it can't come home.
DGF.Raid.furnitureLost: The furniture is lost or abandoned for the night: it can't be taken again, and it makes no more noise.
DGF.Chase.fate.flees: {name} is Already Dead: the Limit has come, so it isn't captured and loses no Turn: it joins the final flight.
DGF.Raid.furnitureInPlay: The furniture is in play: Suspicion +1 at the end of each Turn, even while it's set down.
DGF.Raid.partyOut: The party is out of town: no hunt or chase starts now, not even at dawn.
DGF.Raid.backInTownHint: A mistake: the party never left. The raid goes on as before.
